data.narrative:
Hyperscale Power is a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Daniel Rothmund (PhD ETH Zurich, ex-ABB) and Sami Pettersson (ex-ABB), having raised €5M to date. The valuation universe consists of 9 private peers in Climate & Energy alongside 1 public comparable (LNZA), though direct peer multiples at identical stage and valuation tier are absent in sufficient density.

Given data constraints, Stage-Progression provides the applicable method. Using total raised (€5M) as a base-value proxy and applying a typical Seed-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.5x yields €12M ($12M). This method anchors to the observable transition premium between seed and early growth stages while remaining agnostic to sector-specific volatility. Peer-Median analysis is not applicable; although 9 same-sector peers exist, filtering for matching stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation tier yields insufficient density (need ≥3 datapoints). A broad sector median would introduce uncontrolled variance.

The triangulated range is €11M–€14M ($11M–$14M), centered on €12M ($12M). This reflects a single credible method and carries material uncertainty around (1) whether Seed-stage step-up rates hold in early-stage climate tech given longer capex cycles and (2) absence of narrow peer anchors to stress-test the multiplier. The range should be treated as indicative pending additional comparable data or revenue/product milestones that sharpen the valuation frame.
